Sure, Bill Skarsgård was returning, along with creatives Andy Muschietti and Barbara Muschietti, but what could be gained by having Pennywise chase a new group of kids?
Despite the odds, IT: Welcome to Derry is a fun and terrifying show, one that takes its time building up to the killer clown. It also finds its reason to exist by exploring storylines only briefly mentioned in King's original novel. IT: Welcome to Derry has been confirmed to return for a second season, and when it does, the story will jump backward to an era that will turn the series into something more akin to Boardwalk Empire or Peaky Blinders.

The Spiral The Venice Film Festival has a new guilty pleasure.
The hometown crowd went wild Monday night for the world premiere of The Spiral, a campy, fun Italian horror thriller from director Paolo Strippoli (The Holy Boy, A Classic Horror Story).
Jasmine Trinca (Saint Laurent, The Caiman) stars as Anna, a controlling mother who makes a deal with the devil, in the form of a trench coat-wearing, chain-smoking Valeria Bruni Tedeschi, to save her daughter Alice (Romana Maggiora Vergano) after a gruesome accident. But the agreement sets off a, you guessed it, spiral of macabre events that will end up tearing the family apart. Adriano Giannini plays Anna’s wealthy alpha-male businessman husband, Walter. Andrea Genovese plays their son Tobia.
The twisty genre film, which dips into Grand Guignol territory, with plenty of OTT performances — led by Tedeschi’s glorious turn — may be an outsider for the Golden Lion, but it definitely played for the Venice audience, which gave it a warm and enthusiastic standing ovation, with the director and cast coaxing the crowd to keep clapping past the 9-minute mark.

She got into breakdancing through her husband, a Breakin' fan.

Australia doesn't have much of a B‑girl scene.
